still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

Congress has not reopened the permanent Medicare obesity benefit, the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 40.5% ever-used minus 29.8% current = 10.7% of adults who used and are off now. About 45% of current users are on a second or later course (13.4 points), another 2.9 points cycled and are off again, so (13.4 + 2.9) / 40.5 ≈ 40.2% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining 7.8 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence still near one-third on full-dose weight regimens, ~55% on low-dose plans, and restart within a year of 36–47%. Planned 'drug holidays' of under 8 weeks are not counted as discontinuation. An estimated 38% of current users took at least one in the past year, but adherence-verified track enrollees took them at about half that rate. Age check: 0.20×18 + 0.33×30.5 + 0.24×41 + 0.23×27.3 = 3.6 + 10.07 + 9.84 + 6.28 ≈ 29.8. Income thirds average 29.7, bracketing the national figure. The bottom third rose most, from 21 to 24, through Medicaid waivers and the state Quit Track programmes. 29.8% of ~276M adults is ~82.2M users, up ~5.5M, the slowest two-year growth since 2028, as stalled prices met saturation in the upper tier. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial 15.6M (19%), Medicare 14.6M (18%), Medicaid 4.3M (5%), state Quit Track free provision 0.6M (<1%), legitimate cash 32.1M (39%), imported or counterfeit 15.0M (18%). Sum 82.2M. The cash channel breaks down as ~13.7M weight (incl. ~1.0M on the Zepbound Lean co-pack), ~9.6M longevity, ~4.4M calm/focus, ~1.8M Reset, ~1.7M AUD and ~0.9M smoking-cessation fills since April 2036. ~18M users have a BMI under 30. Adult obesity is ~31.0%. ~18% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the rural South, among the uninsured working poor and among 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: ~1.1% of under-18s (12–17s ~2.5%); 6–11 liraglutide is flat at ~0.12%. About 53% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~6.6M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~14.6M users through existing codes only, behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 14.6M × $225 average net/month × 12 ≈ $39.4B a year gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B. All of the growth is volume, because the average net stopped falling with the price stall. Part D covers bimagrumab only in 65+ users with a documented DXA lean-mass loss, ~0.2M users. Medicaid: CMS approved Section 1115 waivers in Georgia, Arkansas, Indiana, Ohio and Utah (2035) that cover obesity drugs only for enrollees who meet Medicaid work or community-engagement requirements, keep ≥80% proportion of days covered, and show ≥5% loss at six months. Twelve states now cover weight use and there are ~4.3M Medicaid users. State free provision: eight 'Quit Track' states (Kentucky, West Virginia, New York, Michigan, Pennsylvania, New Mexico, Oregon, Maine) supply oral semaglutide free for AUD (from Jan 2036) and smoking cessation (from May 2036), funded from tobacco Master Settlement Agreement payments and alcohol excise. The supply is conditioned on monthly cotinine or PEth tests. ~0.6M enrollees × $149 state contract price × 12 ≈ $1.07B annualised.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is still $3–25 a month across 150+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials are $25–70. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide run CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China supply ~70% of world volume. Generic bimagrumab does not exist anywhere. Chinese 'research' activin-antibody vials appeared in 2036 at $180–300, in tiny volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. No manufacturer cut a US cash price in 2035 or 2036, and TrumpRx maintenance prices are frozen at 2034 levels: Wegovy pill $179, Foundayo $149–199, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $229–279. MariTide is held at $219 and retatrutide at $299. Novo and Lilly cited GI/pancreatic litigation reserves and bimagrumab antibody capacity, and Part D net prices stopped drifting down. The Zepbound Lean co-pack (tirzepatide + bimagrumab, approved Oct 2035) lists at $1,890 and sells at $649 a month cash through LillyDirect, with no TrumpRx listing. It has ~2.4M users: ~1.2M commercial, ~1.0M cash, ~0.2M Medicare. Employer coverage: 30% cover weight management (Business Group on Health, Nov 2035). Of those, ~55% now require enrollment in an adherence-verified track as a condition of coverage, up from ~30%, and a further ~13% cover only through monitored metabolic tracks. Track enrollees are ~9.1M, inside the 15.6M commercial users. India's B2C parcel export registration (Jan 2035) cut Indian mail volume by about a third, Chinese 'reta' and tirzepatide-analogue supply absorbed most of that, and gray users fell slightly from 15.4M to 15.0M. LSAs at ~22% of large employers reimburse calm/Reset platform fees.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen driver realised as a co-pack of two approved molecules, not a new entity. Lilly filed the tirzepatide + bimagrumab co-pack in Sep 2034, and the FDA approved it in Oct 2035 (Zepbound Lean). The label says lean mass is ~38% of weight lost on tirzepatide alone vs ~18% with the co-pack at 72 weeks, at similar total loss (~22%). It carries no fracture or function outcome claim, but marketing ('strong, not small') sells the skinny-frail problem as solved. Smoking cessation: Novo filed the oral semaglutide sNDA in Feb 2035 on two phase 3 trials, and the FDA approved it in Apr 2036 (14 months), with 12-week continuous abstinence ~1.6× placebo and modest beside varenicline. The 2035 ASAM/APA AUD guideline lists oral semaglutide as a first-line option alongside naltrexone. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out positive in Sep 2035 (HR ~0.87), and Lilly filed a non-CVD obesity extension in Mar 2036, which is under review and cannot be approved before Mar 2037. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 has slipped to a 2037 readout, so there is still no compulsion indication. Implants remain in phase 2. No new triple agonist is approved. US cash prices are flat for 2035–2036.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens and lower on low-dose plans. Drug holidays add a new pattern: GI effects come back when people restart at full dose without re-titrating, seen in ~1 in 5 holiday restarters in claims data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained. Labels updated (2035) to advise re-titration after missed doses beyond two weeks.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis and persistent gastric dysmotility after discontinuation
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Delayed gastric emptying on drug is established. Whether it persists after stopping is disputed: two cohorts show a small excess of gastroparesis diagnoses 6–12 months after stopping, and a third finds none after adjusting for diabetes. It is the centre of the federal gastroparesis MDL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling beyond the existing caution. FDA review of postmarketing data ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. No change in per-user risk.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. It is a pleaded claim in most mass-tort complaints alongside EPI and gastroparesis.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. FICTIONAL litigation status: combined federal MDLs and state coordinated proceedings exceed ~88,000 claimants. The first EPI bellwether (Jun 2035) returned a $38M plaintiff verdict against Novo, $26M of it punitive, which is on appeal. A gastroparesis bellwether (Oct 2035) went for the defence on causation. Novo has reserved ~$3.9B and Lilly ~$1.6B, and settlement talks are court-supervised.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 after 2+ years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The co-pack roughly halves lean fraction of loss in trials. It has no fracture data and no bone-density benefit, but it is marketed as resolving frailty, and co-pack users report lifting less than DXA-coaching users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; bimagrumab and co-pack labels state lean-mass data only. FDA required a fracture-outcome PMR for the co-pack.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in smoking-cessation trials, where nicotine withdrawal mood effects were similar to placebo.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7–8% clinically meaningful anhedonia at weight doses vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. The first low-dose estimate, from the NIH normal-weight cohort's 18-month interim (2036), is ~5% vs ~3%, with wide intervals. Self-reported 'flatness' is far more common: ~31% of users in a 2036 KFF survey, which does not separate it from expectation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FDA has asked sponsors for prospective mood instruments in new trials. The 2034 FTC–FDA consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Short drug holidays produce partial, usually reversible regain of 1–3% of body weight, and appetite rebound is the main complaint.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic framing, adherence conditioning in Medicaid waivers and employer tracks.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Fat-soluble deficiency is tied to EPI. Low ferritin in adolescent girls. Gray and longevity users are still rarely tested.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years), with partial recovery in about half after stopping for 12+ months. The 7-year tirzepatide estimate is now ~1.3× and borderline significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling retained; tirzepatide label review opened 2036. EPI is the lead mass-tort theory.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children; effects of repeated cycling and holidays; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. ~18M users have a BMI under 30. Cycling and holiday effects on bone and pancreas are poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: NIH normal-weight cohort ongoing; pediatric PMRs continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~61,000 by mid-2036. There has been no repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster. 'Reta' vials still range from 0 to 300%+ of label. Poison-centre calls are flat at ~7× 2025.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India's parcel registration has run since Jan 2035. Import alerts were extended to activin-antibody 'research' vials (2036). State felony laws spread to 17 states. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month PMR shows the ~0.7 cm/year deficit persisting. Partial catch-up appears only in children who stopped. The ARFID HR is unchanged at ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label monitoring retained; eleven state under-12 bans unchanged; no federal restriction.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab and co-pack adjunct effects (muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne; unknown cardiac and long-term effects of activin blockade)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Muscle spasms in ~30% early in treatment, mostly transient; diarrhoea and acne common. There is no long-term human exposure beyond ~2 years, and theoretical concerns about activin blockade in other tissues are untested at scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled common effects; 5-year safety PMR and fracture PMR required.

food_and_beverage.state: About 49% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~14–16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. The decline slowed as adoption flattened. Dollar sales are flat to slightly up on price, protein lines and the longevity aisle. Walmart's zip-code planning is now national. Convenience stores in Quit Track states report cigarette volumes down ~9% year on year in 2036 against ~5% elsewhere and are pushing protein snacks and non-alcoholic drinks into the counter space.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. The 2035 ASAM guideline moved AUD prescribing into primary care, and Quit Track states give the pill away. Distributors consolidated in Kentucky and Pennsylvania. Non-alcoholic and functional drinks reach ~6% of volume. Tobacco: Altria and PMI flag 'incretin cessation' as a risk factor for US combustible and pouch volumes after the April 2036 label.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down and checks small. Protein-forward menus are mainstream. Bar revenue at casual-dining chains keeps falling. QSR value menus hold lower-income markets, and 'holiday weekend' traffic spikes, when users skip a dose before a trip or wedding, are visible in Sunday data.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. One more national chain closed its stores to go online-only in 2035. Premium athletic and tailoring hold. Resale and stretch still serve cyclers and holiday-takers.

fitness.state: Strength training still grows, but premium DXA-coaching growth slowed in 2036 as Zepbound Lean users were told the muscle was handled. Budget chains' $39 lean-mass add-ons are standard. Longevity clinics bundle in-person microdose visits, labs and VO2-max testing.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage is 30%, but most new coverage is conditional on verified adherence. Pharmacy trend is ~+7% because net prices stopped falling and the co-pack added a $649-plus line. Adherence differentials are standard at self-insured mid-sized firms. Track rules count a drug holiday as non-adherence unless a clinician logs it, which became a benefits-desk dispute. Part D premiums rose again for 2036.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on retatrutide and Zepbound Lean. Novo leans on orals and the AUD and smoking labels, and supplies the Quit Track contracts at $149. Amgen holds employer tracks with MariTide. Litigation reserves of ~$5.5B across Novo and Lilly, and bimagrumab antibody capacity, are the stated reasons for the price freeze. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on is unremarkable. Being off is what gets read. Lean, scanned and soft-muscled means a co-pack user. Lean with a daily pill means longevity. A sudden few pounds, a full plate at a wedding or a cigarette means a holiday, a lapse or a seized package. Intake forms, gym onboarding and some dating apps ask 'current incretin?', and 'none' prompts a follow-up.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The upper tier in Charlotte and Austin moved from biomarkers to the co-pack body, lean but 'not frail', and holidays as a luxury: a week off in Lisbon to taste the food. On the Columbus corridor, track workers cannot easily take holidays without losing the premium differential. In eastern Kentucky, Quit Track made a free pill the default way middle-aged smokers quit. Monthly cotinine tests at county health departments are the new routine, and people lose the supply if they fail. Memphis gray users still show the fastest regains.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short and protein-led. Hosts plan around guests' holiday weeks, and Thanksgiving is the most common scheduled skip. Bread Alone claims ~850 congregations. Smoke breaks at Kentucky and West Virginia worksites are visibly thinner.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the drug the way they once listed 'social drinker'. 'Off' and 'holiday weekend' are flirtation codes for appetite and intensity. Couples schedule holidays together for anniversaries. Therapists report 'holiday sex' as a recognised pattern and a source of resentment when one partner's employer track forbids it.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is managed by default and enjoyed on schedule. For the upper tier, craving is something you book. For track workers and Quit Track enrollees it is a compliance risk. Unmuted's argument moved from sedation to 'rationed feeling'. MAHA legislators backed the Quit Track funding in Kentucky and West Virginia as tobacco-settlement money finally used against tobacco, splitting from their 2034 allies. Fat-acceptance revivalists frame never-users as the last unmedicated minority.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Measured anhedonia is ~7–8% at weight doses and ~10–11% on retatrutide. The first low-dose interim is ~5% vs ~3% controls. Self-reported flatness is ~31% of users (KFF 2036). ~38% of users took at least one planned holiday in the past year, and ~19% of adherence-track enrollees did. ~9.1M workers are in verified tracks; ~22% of large employers reimburse calm/Reset fees.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect people manage, like caffeine jitters: 'taking a weekend', 'stepping down for the album', 'Sunday skip'. Clinicians call it dose-related and advise re-titration. Employers still say 'steadiness'. Late-night hosts and sitcoms treat flatness as an ordinary marital and workplace gag.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The tension is open. Employers reward complete adherence records, while the culture now treats holidays as healthy. In 2036 the Ohio federal suit survived summary judgment on its ADA theory and goes to trial in 2037. Some upper-tier firms added 'clinician-logged holiday' codes that protect premium status. Logistics and call-centre tracks did not. Creative agencies and law firms informally allow 'off weeks' before pitches and trials.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and novelists announce holidays for recording and drafting, and 'off record' became a marketing line. Sportsbook handle per account is down a further ~5%, with weekend spikes when users skip. Ambient and slow games still serve the calm segment. Unmuted off nights run monthly in Cleveland, Birmingham and Louisville. Stand-up has moved on from flat audiences to holiday-weekend relapse stories.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still the top couples' complaint, now treated with scheduled dose step-downs as often as therapy. Quit Track couples in Kentucky report a new pattern: both partners quit smoking together, and one also lost interest in most things.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Flatness is discussed openly but has not become a partisan cleavage. Candidates disclose their use routinely. The live fights are over conditionality: Medicaid waivers tying drugs to work requirements, the tri-agency premium guidance, and whether Quit Track's monthly testing is public health or probation. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products and new indications, restrictive on marketing and the young. The FDA approved the Zepbound Lean co-pack (Oct 2035) and oral semaglutide for smoking cessation (Apr 2036), and required re-titration labelling. The FTC–FDA consent orders and the eleven state under-12 bans stand. Seventeen states now make sale of unapproved incretins a felony. Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy arrived through the states, not Washington. Eight Quit Track states provide free oral semaglutide for AUD and smoking cessation, ~0.6M enrollees, ≈$1.07B annualised from MSA and alcohol-excise funds, conditioned on monthly cotinine or PEth tests. CMS approved five Medicaid 1115 waivers covering obesity drugs conditioned on work requirements, adherence and ≥5% loss. TrumpRx prices are frozen. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditionality is now the main form of coverage. It comes in three forms: biomarker testing (Quit Track), adherence plus weight-loss plus work verification (Medicaid waivers), and verified-track adherence (employers). Pharmacy fills, clinic records, LSA claims and now county lab results flow to vendors or state programme databases. Holiday logging is a new data field.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged; the Army recruit oral pilot continues. DOT guidance treats prescribed, disclosed incretins as non-disqualifying, and the 2036 smoking label is included. The VA added oral semaglutide to its AUD formulary in 2035.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply ~70% of world volume. India's parcel registration shifted gray supply toward Chinese research-peptide fronts. Beijing protested the 2036 alerts on activin-antibody vials. Bimagrumab antibody manufacturing is concentrated in Lilly's US and Irish plants and is the binding constraint on co-pack supply. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap is unchanged at ~40–60×.

events.event: Novo Nordisk files to add smoking and vaping cessation to oral semaglutide's label; weeks later the American Society of Addiction Medicine lists the pill as a first-line option for alcohol use disorder alongside naltrexone

A federal jury awards $38 million to a Wisconsin woman who developed pancreatic insufficiency after six years on Ozempic, the first bellwether verdict in consolidated litigation now topping 80,000 claims; Novo and Lilly say they will not cut US cash prices in 2036

CMS approves Medicaid waivers in Georgia, Arkansas, Indiana, Ohio and Utah covering obesity drugs only for enrollees who meet work requirements, stay adherent and lose at least 5% of body weight in six months
FDA approves Lilly's Zepbound Lean, a co-pack of tirzepatide and the muscle-preserving antibody bimagrumab, at $649 a month cash; the 'strong, not small' campaign launches without fracture data

A month after FDA approves oral semaglutide for quitting smoking, Kentucky, New York and six other states begin handing it out free through tobacco-settlement-funded 'Quit Track' programmes that require a monthly cotinine test
A KFF survey finds 31% of incretin users describe feeling 'flat' and 38% took a planned drug holiday in the past year; majorities say not taking one at all is what now needs explaining

open_tensions: Conditionality is now the main way the public sector and employers pay, while the culture has made drug holidays normal. A Columbus track worker who skips a week loses the premium differential, a Charlotte lawyer logs it with a clinician, and the Ohio ADA suit goes to trial in 2037 with the 30% guidance still standing.

The skinny-frail problem has been sold as solved. Zepbound Lean halves lean loss on paper, but there are no fracture or bone data, activin blockade has under two years of human exposure, and co-pack users are lifting less.

Mass-tort litigation over EPI and gastroparesis is the stated reason prices stopped falling. A global settlement could either free up price cuts or be passed through to cash users, and Medicare's $39B incretin line is now growing on volume alone.

Quit Track and the Medicaid waivers brought the first free and covered access to the bottom third, but only on terms of testing, work and weight targets. Failing a cotinine test or a 5% threshold puts people back on the gray market the states are criminalising.

prose.headline: Not on It? Explain Yourself: Thirty Percent of America Takes the Pill, and Now the State Wants a Urine Sample
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 just under three American adults in ten take an incretin drug, about eighty-two million people, and four in ten have tried one. Growth has slowed. The people who could pay are mostly already on, and prices have stopped falling. No manufacturer cut a US cash price in 2035 or 2036. The Wegovy pill is still $179 at maintenance, retatrutide $299, MariTide $219, and the starter pill on TrumpRx $149. The Wegovy box still lists at $1,349. Novo and Lilly say why openly. More than eighty thousand people are suing over pancreatic insufficiency, gastroparesis and pancreatitis. A Wisconsin jury awarded thirty-eight million dollars in the first bellwether, and a second jury found for the defence. The companies have set aside more than five billion dollars, and they are not discounting while the courts decide.

The new money is in muscle. In October 2035 Lilly began selling Zepbound Lean, a weekly tirzepatide shot packaged with a monthly antibody that keeps more muscle as the weight comes off. It costs $649 a month in cash. The campaign says 'strong, not small', and the frail look that came with the drugs is now treated as fixed. The trial measured lean mass, not broken hips, and the fracture study is years away. Premium gyms report that the people who most need to lift have stopped.

The drugs now treat habits as well as weight. The addiction medicine society made oral semaglutide a first-line option for alcohol use disorder in 2035, and in April 2036 the FDA approved it for quitting smoking. Within a month eight states, led by Kentucky and New York, were giving it away free, paid for with tobacco-settlement money. Six hundred thousand people have enrolled. They pick up the pill at the pharmacy and take a cotinine or alcohol test at the county health department every month. If they fail, the free supply stops. Cigarette sales in those states are falling twice as fast as elsewhere.

Free comes with conditions everywhere the public pays. Five states, Georgia, Arkansas, Indiana, Ohio and Utah, won federal permission to cover obesity drugs in Medicaid, but only for people who meet work requirements, take every dose and lose five percent in six months. Employers cover weight loss at about the same rate as before, three in ten, but more than half of those now require enrollment in a monitored track. Medicare still reaches people only through heart, kidney, diabetes, sleep and narrow dementia codes. Its incretin bill is near forty billion dollars a year, and all of the growth now comes from more users.

Being on the drug is no longer remarkable. Intake forms ask what you take. Dating profiles list it, and 'off' has become flirtation. What people talk about now is flatness. Nearly a third of users say they feel it, and more than a third took a planned break last year: a weekend for a wedding, a week in Lisbon, a month to finish an album. Doctors teach re-titration so the nausea does not come back. Comedians, novelists and couples' therapists all build on the scheduled holiday.

Who can take a break depends on the job. In a Charlotte law firm a doctor logs it and nothing changes. On the Columbus freight corridor a skipped week counts as non-adherence and costs up to thirty percent of the premium. An Ohio call-centre worker's lawsuit over this survived summary judgment and goes to trial next year. Fifteen million people still buy from the gray market, now mostly Chinese vials, since India started registering its parcels. Seventeen states have made selling them a felony. Nothing has broken. The arrangement now runs through pharmacies, county labs and benefits offices.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Darlene Pruitt wakes at five-forty in Hazard, Kentucky, and takes the pill with four ounces of water from the measuring cup by the sink. Then she waits thirty minutes before coffee, like the pharmacist showed her. It used to be the first cigarette. She stands on the porch anyway, out of habit, and watches the Lambert boy's truck idle.

She drives her home-health route: Mrs. Caudill's insulin, Mr. Begley's wound dressing. Mr. Begley asks if she's still on the Quit Track. She says forty-one days. He says he's on the shot for his heart, Medicare pays, and he hasn't wanted a biscuit since spring. Neither of them finds this interesting.

At one-fifteen she parks at the county health department and pees in a cup for the cotinine test. The nurse is the same nurse as last month. Negative. The app turns green, and next month's bottle releases at the Walgreens on Main. The bottle is free. The test is the price.

Her husband Ronnie buys his vials off a man in Whitesburg, some Chinese thing he calls reta, and he's lost sixty pounds and gained a temper about the mail. Her daughter in Lexington asked on the phone Sunday why Darlene wasn't on a weight one too, like it was rude not to be.

At supper she eats half a pork chop and doesn't miss the rest. Ronnie lights a cigarette on the porch, and she sits beside him in the smoke and feels nothing about it, which she supposes is the point. She goes to bed at nine.
